nodes.title: Brown’s 2-adic determinant argument
nodes.statement: Every nonempty Hoffman cut matrix M_{N,l} is invertible over Q. The elementary criterion is: for a rational square matrix, if every below-diagonal entry has 2-adic valuation≥1 and each diagonal entry realizes its column’s minimum valuation, which is≤0, then the determinant is nonzero. Rescale each column by a power of two to make that minimum zero; reduction modulo 2 is upper triangular with nonzero diagonal. Brown’s coefficient estimates and leading-cut computation verify these hypotheses.

nodes.title: The motivic Hoffman basis
nodes.statement: For each N≥0, {ζ^m_desc(k) : k is a {2,3}-word of weight N} is a Q-basis of H_N; the empty word is the weight-zero basis and weight one has empty basis. The level induction proves independence via the invertible cut matrices. The number of these words is d_N, matching the Hilbert-series upper bound; hence H=H_MT^+ and every motivic MZV is a rational linear combination of the 2/3 values.
proofSteps: Induct on weight and level. A relation in highest level is sent by all D_r to lower-weight relations; invertibility of M_{N,l} forces its top-level coefficients to vanish. Descend the level filtration.
The surviving level-zero all-two value is nonzero by its period. Compare independent word count with the upper bound dim H_N≤d_N to prove spanning and equality with the ambient algebra.

nodes.title: Quartic local continuation and reflection
nodes.statement: First define the local analytic ratio P_loc(s) near s=1 on a slit neighbourhood, with U₁(s)=Γ(1/8)²/Γ(1/2)·₂F₁(1/8,1/8;1/2;1−s⁴) and U₂(s)=Γ(5/8)²/Γ(3/2)·(s⁴−1)^(1/2)₂F₁(5/8,5/8;3/2;1−s⁴). On the branch continued from real s>1, P_loc=i/√2·(U₁+cot(π/8)U₂)/(U₁−cot(π/8)U₂). For the marked geometric normalization based on the ray t=i·s, pull this formula back by s=−it to a slit neighbourhood of t=i: there p(t)=P_loc(−it). Thus the γ₁ square-root sign change sends p to −1/(2p). This uses the equal parameters corrected by E2. In the distinct based chart at t=1, γ₄ acts by p↦1−1/(2(p−1))=(3−2p)/(2−2p), so its centred local coordinate is p−1. Do not identify the two based loops or their unshifted local coordinates (E4).

Pull the local formula back by t=i·s, so its large-parameter ray is the normalizing ray t=i√2 and its slit neighbourhood is at t=i. Since (−it)⁴=t⁴, the pulled series and the chosen logarithmic branch agree there. The square-root sign change supplies the γ₁ reflection; with the infinity translation it fixes the additive constant by Hartmann Proposition 4.25.

Keep the γ₄ chart separate. Conjugating R(p)=−1/(2p) by T(p)=p+1 gives T R T⁻¹(p)=1−1/(2(p−1)), the γ₄ action already computed from its matrix. Hartmann’s Theorem 4.29 proof treats the images of these distinct based loops as equal; E4 records the correction to that argument.

At U₂=0 the γ₁ local fixed point is p=i/√2; the γ₄ fixed points are 1±i/√2 in its based geometric coordinate.
